params.requirement: Chooses one model from a catalogue for a stated need and names the reason in one sentence. Rare calls, a few kilobytes in, a short JSON answer out; careful reading and exact instruction-following matter far more than speed or price.

translator_model.description: LLM_REGISTRY_TRANSLATOR_MODEL -- the START VALUE of the translator's model. The registry never resolves it: a registry that needed its own resolution to translate could not repair one, so this cell stays on what it was born on: no edge brings a params message into it, only questions from ./hand.

api_key.description: Provider API key. Ships empty: the registry boots, resolves and pushes without one, and every translation fails loudly into the journal until the colony grants it a credential. Deprecated, removed in 0.63.0: name a grant in credential_grant_id instead (#801).

credential_grant_id.description: GH #801: the grant this cell presents to get its provider credential SEALED from an access hive instead of carrying a key. It ships EMPTY, which is no grant at all; whoever grows the cell (the builder recipe or the colony's own template) sets it through `override_params`, and the credential then arrives over the credential v-lane and is opened in RAM only. Immutable: a new grant is a new instance.

external_timeout_ms_row.description: GH #1097: not read by the cell -- the catalogue row its `external_timeout_ms` and `cell.message_timeout` are derived from (the timeout chain, docs/cell-types.md § llm): the row of the model this cell is born on. A manifest that bears it on another row derives both again from that row.

messages.description: Not required (GH #1061): the sealed credential box the access hive delivers on `in_sealed` carries `sealed` and nothing else, and a required key here would refuse it at delivery.

description.purpose: The translator of the registry (GH #858): one prose requirement and the active catalogue in, one `{"model_id", "reason"}` out. It is asked ONLY when a (requirement, catalogue) pair has no translation yet, and its answer is a candidate, not a decision -- `hand` checks it against the catalogue and stores it as a row, and every resolution after that reads the row.
description.use_when: Inside the llm-registry hive, behind `hand`. Nothing else addresses it: `params.ports` of the hive is empty, and the only edges into and out of it are the two internal ones to `./hand`.
description.not_in_scope: It resolves nothing and is resolved by nothing: its own model is a start value (the environment key LLM_REGISTRY_TRANSLATOR_MODEL), and no `update` edge of the registry reaches it -- so a broken translator can never stand between the registry and a repair. When it fails or answers outside the catalogue, every subscriber keeps the resolution it had. It keeps no history: each question carries the whole catalogue, and the answer is stored by `hand`, not here.
